finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF in /fetch2: the user-supplied url query parameter is fetched with requests.get after only a scheme check, so any internal or metadata address is reachable, and redirects are followed by default.

trace.note: url read from request.args with no authentication required
is_http_url only checks urlparse(url).scheme in (http, https); no host, IP, or allowlist check
requests.get fetches the attacker URL with default redirect following; first 200 bytes of body returned to caller

finding.guards_checked: Scheme-only check (validators.py:7) does not restrict host. No hostname allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local IP filtering, no allow_redirects=False, no post-redirect re-validation. Timeout of 5s is not a security control.

verdict.guard_found: none on the /fetch2 path. The only check is is_http_url at views.py:20, which calls validators.py:7 and tests only the scheme. No hostname, IP, or allowlist check, and requests.get at views.py:22 has no allow_redirects=False, so redirects are followed. The stronger is_safe_url guard (validators.py:10-18) is used only by /fetch (views.py:12), not /fetch2.
verdict.reason: The url comes from an unauthenticated request.args value (views.py:19), passes only the scheme-only is_http_url check (views.py:20, validators.py:7), and is fetched with requests.get at views.py:22 with default redirect following, returning the first 200 bytes; the candidate's trace matches the code exactly.

finding.claim: DNS-rebinding TOCTOU in /fetch: is_safe_url resolves the hostname and checks every returned IP, but requests.get performs a second, independent DNS resolution and connects to whatever address it receives, so an attacker-controlled domain can pass the check with a public IP and then resolve to 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, or an RFC-1918 host for the actual fetch.
finding.sink: views.py:14 requests.get(url, timeout=5, allow_redirects=False) (connection to the second, unvalidated DNS resolution)

trace.note: url read from request.args with no authentication required
is_safe_url gate applied before the fetch
urlparse; scheme restricted to http/https and hostname required
first DNS resolution via socket.getaddrinfo; result is only used for the check
each resolved IP checked for is_private, is_loopback, is_link_local, is_reserved
requests.get re-resolves the hostname in urllib3 and connects to the returned IP, which the check never saw

finding.guards_checked: Scheme restriction (validators.py:12) and hostname-present check (validators.py:12) present. All resolved addresses checked for private/loopback/link-local/reserved (validators.py:14-17). allow_redirects=False (views.py:14) closes redirect-based bypass. Timeout 5s. Missing: connection pinning to the validated IP, or connect-time IP check, so the check and the fetch can resolve differently. Practical impact limited by 200-byte response truncation and rebinding timing window.

verdict.guard_found: none. validators.py:12 is a scheme and hostname check, and validators.py:14-17 checks resolved IPs, but nothing pins the connection to the validated IP. views.py:14 calls requests.get(url) with the hostname, so urllib3 resolves it again. views.py:14 also sets allow_redirects=False, which closes only the redirect path. Neither guard closes the rebinding TOCTOU.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: url comes from unauthenticated request.args at views.py:11, is_safe_url at views.py:12 resolves via getaddrinfo at validators.py:14 and checks the IPs at validators.py:16, and requests.get at views.py:14 performs a separate DNS resolution with no pinned IP. Nothing in the path closes the gap, so the rebinding TOCTOU is real. The response is truncated to 200 bytes (views.py:14), which limits impact but does not refute the finding.
